newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIAN CLUBS PENALISED BECAUSE OF ICEBOUND PITCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIAN CLUBS PENALISED BECAUSE OF ICEBOUND PITCHES.

text.p: Seven Russian premier league teams, including each of the three newly promoted clubs, must play their first two home fixtures of the 1997 season at neutral grounds after failing to install undersoil heating.

League vice-president Leonid Lipovoi said on Thursday that the seven were being punished for failing to meet a league ruling to install heating to combat Russian soccer's perennial problem of icy pitches in early and late season.

"It's a gross violation of the agreement we came to in December and the league is determined to put an end to their sloppiness," Lipovoi said. "We gave them money and other support and they unceremoniously broke the agreement they voted for."
If they do not install undersoil heating by September 27, the clubs will be docked six points and play their final two home matches in the 18-team league at away grounds.

The seven are KamAZ Naberezhniye Chelny, Krylya Sovietov Samara, Rostselmash Rostov and Baltika Kaliningrad as well as the three newly promoted sides -- Fakel Voronezh, Shinnik Yaroslavl and Dynamo-Gazovik from Tyumen in frozen Siberia.
The 1997 season kicks off on March 16 and will end on November 9.

Some of the big Russian clubs, mainly in Moscow, have lobbied for a west European-style calendar, playing from autumn to spring. But smaller teams complain that soccer is impractical during Russia's long, hard winters.
